records.title: Lifetime children enquiry and dated figure
records.anchor: If the Querent should ever have Children?; Die Jupiter 11 Iune 1635
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: The question asks whether the querent should ever have children. The figure records 11 June 1635, Thursday, 2:30 P.M., with Jupiter as the astrological hour ruler.

records.title: Barren and indifferent sign testimonies
records.anchor: The ascendant is here Virgo a barren Signe; a Signe of indifferency
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: Lilly calls the Virgo Ascendant barren, the Capricorn fifth sign indifferent for this question, the Moon's sign barren, and Saturn in Sagittarius and Mercury in Gemini rather barren than fruitful.

records.title: Afflictions and shared fifth/sixth ruler
records.anchor: Saturn Lord of the fift house is Retrograde; who is Lord of the sixt, as well as of the fift
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: Saturn is retrograde; Moon in Mars's terms squares Saturn; Mercury in Saturn's terms is with Mars and goes to Saturn opposition; Saturn rules both fifth and sixth; the South Node occupies the Ascendant. Lilly treats these as adverse testimonies.

records.title: Past nonconception and lifelong negative judgment
records.anchor: neither had been ever yet conceived; the first, tenth and fourth houses
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
conditions: Lilly found the preceding negative configuration

all: Lilly found the preceding negative configuration

records.assertion: On the listed testimonies Lilly says the querent had not conceived and would never conceive, describing her as naturally barren; first/tenth/fourth affliction makes him infer the impediment was longstanding and would continue.

records.title: Jupiter contact would soften the categorical negative
records.anchor: Had I found Jupiter either fortunating the cusp of the fift house
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: Lilly would have been less categorical had Jupiter fortunated the fifth cusp, aspected the Ascendant ruler or Saturn, or had reception existed between Saturn and Jupiter or between Jupiter and Mercury.
exceptions: These are stated counterfactual alternatives; not an assertion that they occurred.

records.title: Reception-qualified collection would soften judgment
records.anchor: any collection of light from Mercury to Saturn; received Saturn or Mercury
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
conditions: A planet collects light from Mercury to Saturn
That collector receives Saturn or Mercury

all: A planet collects light from Mercury to Saturn
That collector receives Saturn or Mercury

records.assertion: Collection of light from Mercury to Saturn, with the collecting planet receiving Saturn or Mercury, would also have made Lilly less categorical.
exceptions: Counterfactual in this worked narrative; not an observed successful exception.

records.title: No promising testimony in the author's assessment
records.anchor: when I found no one promising testimony
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: Lilly says he found no promising testimony and therefore judged against conception or children; this is his assessment of this figure, not this audit's independent exhaustive chart evaluation.

records.title: Reported illness and source-body attribution
records.anchor: very sickly, and extreamly afflicted with the Wind and Cholick
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: The account describes the querent as sickly, with wind and colic in belly/small guts and head pain; Lilly links these to Moon–Saturn, Mercury–Saturn/Mars and the South Node, and cites the Mercury-in-Gemini body table on printed119.

records.title: Reported bodily mark: navel
records.anchor: Shee affirmed, that the Moles of her Body did correspond
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: One mole close by the navel; the sentence does not explicitly assign a separate astrological cause to this first item.

records.title: Reported bodily mark: right_ankle
records.anchor: Shee affirmed, that the Moles of her Body did correspond
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: One on the right ankle, assigned to Aquarius on the sixth cusp.

records.title: Reported bodily mark: right_knee_inner_thigh
records.anchor: Shee affirmed, that the Moles of her Body did correspond
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: One toward the right knee on the inner side of the thigh, assigned to Saturn, lord of sixth, in Sagittarius.

records.title: Reported bodily mark: moon_virgo_member_unspecified
records.anchor: Shee affirmed, that the Moles of her Body did correspond
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: One in or near the member signified by the Moon in Virgo; the anatomical member is not named in this sentence.

records.title: Reported bodily mark: right_arm
records.anchor: Shee affirmed, that the Moles of her Body did correspond
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: A scar or mole on the outside of the right arm, assigned to Mercury, Ascendant ruler, in Gemini.

records.title: Consult nativity for a categorical negative
records.anchor: When you find a Question that is so peremptory in the negative
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
conditions: A strongly negative horary judgment of this kind

all: A strongly negative horary judgment of this kind

records.assertion: For a question so categorical in the negative, enquire birth time, cast the nativity, compare radix with question and use discretion.

records.title: Natal barrenness takes precedence in the stated comparison
records.anchor: if the Radix affirme Barrennesse
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: Lilly states that if the radix affirms barrenness, no promising horary question can contradict that signification.

records.title: First-question Ascendant resemblance claim
records.anchor: I meane in their first Question; found by experience
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: Lilly says that in a person's first question he usually finds the same Ascendant triplicity as the nativity, and often the same sign and degree; he attributes this to his experience.

records.title: Gemini–Libra–Aquarius illustration
records.anchor: for if Gemini ascend in the Nativity
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: Gemini rising in a nativity, with Libra or Aquarius rising in a horary question, illustrates the same-triplicity claim.

records.title: Child-sex and delivery-time enquiry
records.anchor: If one were with Child of a Male or Female; 7 Apri 1645
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: The second figure asks whether the child is male or female and when delivery will occur, dated 7 April 1645 at 2:15 P.M. Its central labels place Moon beside both day and hour.

records.assertion: Lilly says he used the plurality of masculine or feminine testimonies of the proper significators to resolve this example.

records.title: Eight-to-four conclusion and reported male birth
records.anchor: eight testimonies; but four; and so it proved
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: The printed tally is eight male testimonies and four female. Lilly says he therefore judged a male child, adding that it proved so.

records.title: Movable signs tempered by slow Saturn
records.anchor: because Saturn Lord of the fift is a ponderous Planet
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: The movable fifth sign Capricorn and Aries containing the first/fifth rulers suggest a short time, but Lilly gives much weight to slow, ponderous Saturn and to Moon in the sign of the fifth.

records.title: Moon–Saturn square distance
records.anchor: Locus Saturn in 24 37 Aries; Locus Moon in 9 50 Capricorn
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: The table gives Saturn 24°37′ Aries and Moon 9°50′ Capricorn, both cardinal signs; the remaining distance of Moon to Saturn's square is 14°47′.

records.title: Mercury–Saturn conjunction distance
records.anchor: Saturn 24 37 Aries; Mercury 11 00 Aries; Distance13
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: The second table gives Saturn 24°37′ Aries and Mercury 11°00′ Aries; their difference is 13°37′.

records.title: Difference of distances and local degree-to-week rule
records.anchor: one degree and ten minutes; for every degree one week
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: The two distances differ by 1°10′. Lilly assigns one week to every degree and judges delivery about fourteen weeks after the question.

records.title: Reported delivery on 11 July
records.anchor: she was delivered the eleventh of July following
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: Lilly reports delivery on 11 July following the 7 April question.

records.title: Mars and Mercury transits reported at delivery
records.anchor: Mars transited the degree ascending; the opposite place of the Moon
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: The narrative says Mars transited the question's Ascendant degree, and Mercury the opposite place of the question Moon, described as the tenth degree of Cancer.

records.title: Reported exact Sun square and Moon–Mercury conjunction
records.anchor: Sun the same day is in 27.48 Cancer; in perfect square
records.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not a diplomatic quotation
records.assertion: The narrative gives Sun 27°48′ Cancer on that day and calls this a perfect square to its figure position; it also reports Moon in Cancer conjunct Mercury. The figure itself reads Sun 27°52′.
